searchText: hi there 👋 . is anybody working on London and Merge updates to the yellow paper? what is the broad view on supporting the yellow paper moving forward? <@519796549279023105>, <@583892532644151312> had done some recent YP updates, but I don't know if he or anyone had planned to do a full overhaul for The Merge. Folks here have been working on a python spec for Ethereum, see: https://ethereum.github.io/execution-specs/ > what is the broad view on supporting the yellow paper moving forward? re: this, it's not clear to me what the consensus is 😅 the YP has been hard to find maintainers for, but some people really like it, so it might get maintained. That said, it's always a "late" view of the protocol, as EIPs don't get specified using it. <@552133098075193354> thanks for the response! i saw that <@583892532644151312> mentioned that he currently doesn’t have capacity for it in one of the recent issues. was just curious if anything changed or smb aware of any progress on it. i will confess to feeling a tiny bit sentimental here as it was my entry point to Ethereum. i also learnt about a couple of cases where devs were referencing YP as the current source of truth. that’s why i would suggest raising the question of YP support on some kind of a public forum (twitter, reddit, maybe even in this discord) with two possible paths forward: 1. the community has _enough_ demand for the YP’s format and we find some bandwidth to contribute. the only problem i envision here is defining the _enough_ threshold 2. EF issues an “official” deprecation notice for the YP on public channels and adds a similar notice to the current repos/hosted documents and points to `execution-specs` instead. wdyt? Thanks for the context! Re: (1), I'd _like_ to see it (and could perhaps see the EF providing a small grant if someone was really keen to do this but lacked funding?), but historically it's been hard to find people who want to do this work 😅 Spec work is pretty thankless, and so we sort of end up going with whoever shows up. Re: (2), it's not really "the EF" who'd make this call, but I suspect more "AllCoreDevs" (i.e. the set of all client teams + folks involved with protocol work). That would be my preferred option (see: https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/core-eips-in-an-executable-spec-world/8640) but I don't think we quite have the consensus to move forward here (and EELS still needs a bit of polish AIUI). That said, I'm happy to bring this up on calls once the python spec is finalized and we feel like it's the right time to move forward. that makes sense, appreciate the clarification and your intent to bring up this issue on ACD call <:PepeLove:877013138065747968> i’ve launched a twitter poll with whatever tiny audience i’ve got. hope to get some additional context whether people have interest in YP being supported. i think there are some people interested to support YP if there’s demand for it https://twitter.com/r_krasiuk/status/1613645358814605312

excerpts.author: timbeiko
excerpts.content:
<@519796549279023105>, <@583892532644151312> had done some recent YP updates, but I don't know if he or anyone had planned to do a full overhaul for The Merge. 

Folks here have been working on a python spec for Ethereum, see: https://ethereum.github.io/execution-specs/

excerpts.author: timbeiko
excerpts.content:
> what is the broad view on supporting the yellow paper moving forward?
re: this, it's not clear to me what the consensus is 😅  the YP has been hard to find maintainers for, but some people really like it, so it might get maintained. That said, it's always a "late" view of the protocol, as EIPs don't get specified using it.

excerpts.author: closer__
excerpts.content:
<@552133098075193354> thanks for the response! i saw that <@583892532644151312> mentioned that he currently doesn’t have capacity for it in one of the recent issues. was just curious if anything changed or smb aware of any progress on it. 

i will confess to feeling a tiny bit sentimental here as it was my entry point to Ethereum. i also learnt about a couple of cases where devs were referencing YP as the current source of truth. that’s why i would suggest raising the question of YP support on some kind of a public forum (twitter, reddit, maybe even in this discord) with two possible paths forward:
1. the community has _enough_ demand for the YP’s format and we find some bandwidth to contribute. the only problem i envision here is defining the _enough_ threshold
2. EF issues an “official” deprecation notice for the YP on public channels and adds a similar notice to the current repos/hosted documents and points to `execution-specs` instead. 

wdyt?

excerpts.author: timbeiko
excerpts.content:
Thanks for the context! 

Re: (1), I'd _like_ to see it (and could perhaps see the EF providing a small grant if someone was really keen to do this but lacked funding?), but historically it's been hard to find people who want to do this work 😅  Spec work is pretty thankless, and so we sort of end up going with whoever shows up. 

Re: (2), it's not really "the EF" who'd make this call, but I suspect more "AllCoreDevs" (i.e. the set of all client teams + folks involved with protocol work). That would be my preferred option (see: https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/core-eips-in-an-executable-spec-world/8640) but I don't think we quite have the consensus to move forward here (and EELS still needs a bit of polish AIUI). That said, I'm happy to bring this up on calls once the python spec is finalized and we feel like it's the right time to move forward.
